accepts.because: one closed session as a single write batch; the ledger is keyed on the promoted session_id and a batch without one cannot be told apart from its own repeat

emits.because: one message per turn of the batch, for the memory hive's turn-write ingress

description.purpose: Scope marker of the drain hive: the adapter that turns one closed session - handed out by a collector as ONE write batch - into N single-turn episodes on the memory hive's turn-write ingress, plus the ledger that makes a second delivery a skip. It sits BEFORE the hive's writer port and outside the hive (GH #101, R-MD-1): the memory hive is not changed by a single line.
description.use_when: One per talky whose closed sessions should reach the central memory. Wire the two ports in the SAME mutation that instantiates it: the talky's 'write' route into ./drain as lane in_batch, and ./drain's 'episode' route into the memory hive on its in_episode lane.
description.contract_in: Every message whose `hop.route` starts with `in_`. One lane is in use: in_batch — one closed session as a single write batch. The caller must promote `session_id` into `context` on its own edge; the ledger is keyed on it and a batch without one cannot be told apart from its own repeat.
description.contract_out: `episode` — one message per turn of the batch, for the memory hive's turn-write ingress, leaving through the hive path. The ledger write (`lstore`) stays inside: that a second delivery is a skip is this hive's promise, not something a caller arranges.
description.not_in_scope: No extraction, no summarising, no recall, no LLM call - the write path is synchronous and model-free by spec. No second write path into memory: everything goes through the existing writer, which is the point of the adapter. No session lifecycle of its own; the keeper closes the session and the collector produces the batch.
